details.formulaDescription: Let i = gradientPercent / 100. Metabolic cost Cr = 155.4 i^5 − 30.4 i^4 − 43.3 i^3 + 46.3 i^2 + 19.5 i + 3.6 joules per kilogram per metre, the fifth-order polynomial fitted to treadmill running between gradients of −0.45 and +0.45. costRatio = Cr / 3.6, where 3.6 is the flat cost. flatEquivalentPaceSeconds = round(actualPaceSecondsPerKm / costRatio). A positive gradient adds cost, so the flat-equivalent pace is faster than the actual pace; a moderate negative gradient reduces cost, so the flat-equivalent pace is slower.
assumptions: The model comes from treadmill running by ten elite mountain runners and applies to steady running between −45% and +45% gradient.
Flat-equivalent pace means the flat pace with the same modelled metabolic cost; it is not a predicted race performance.
The model assumes a constant gradient over the segment; real courses vary continuously.
Downhill cost saving in the model is not adjusted for braking, eccentric muscle damage, technical terrain or fatigue.
Altitude, heat, wind, surface and body mass are outside the model.
The tool does not give medical or coaching advice.
details.rounding: Cost to three decimal places in joules per kilogram per metre; cost ratio to three decimal places; flat-equivalent pace to the nearest whole second per kilometre. The final pace is computed from the unrounded ratio.
